notes_for_us: A twenty-kilobyte design brief and the layout content is six sentences. The triage rule held up better than I expected - the mechanics array is long and that is correct - but nothing in the skill tells you how to size the build against a prompt like this. The user asked for a vertical slice; the handoff has no way to say 'the first zone only', so scope lives in a note.

A turn-based RPG fights on a dedicated arena that is neither field nor dungeon, and there is no option or shape for it. The genre note says turn-based combat barely changes the layout, which is true of the overworld and false of the battle stage - the prompt spends a whole paragraph on that space.

Same again for the side sport: blitzball-likes are a venue with a playing surface and a crowd, and reaching Sports or Entertainment for it would mean a second shape, which the one-shape rule forbids. A minigame venue inside a larger game has nowhere to go.

The prompt names its zones as palette examples, not as a sequence, and I had to decide whether three named moods are three zones. That decision sets the P4 count and nothing records how confident it was.
